title: 3. Effects of repeated low-dose maternal lipopolysaccharide exposure during the periconception period on ewe immune responses and lamb performance.
content:
Abstract
Gram-negative bacterial endotoxins can impair reproduction through activation of innate immune responses. However, the effects of low-dose endotoxin exposure during the periconception period on maternal immune function and lamb performance remain unclear. This study evaluated repeated low-dose lipopolysaccharide (LPS) challenges prior to breeding on maternal immune responses, reproductive outcomes, and lamb performance. Thirty multiparous Rambouillet ewes (2 to 8 yr of age; 61 ± 6 kg) were stratified by age and body weight (BW) and assigned to receive subcutaneous injections of saline (CON), 1.5 µg/kg BW LPS (LOW), or 3.0 µg/kg BW LPS (HIGH) on d 5, 10, and 15 of a synchronized estrous cycle. Blood samples and rectal temperatures were collected at 0, 2, 4, 6, 12, and 24 h for progesterone, cortisol, complete blood counts, and febrile response. Data were analyzed using mixed models with repeated measures. Progesterone concentrations confirmed estrous synchronization and were similar among treatments on d 5 and 10; however, serum progesterone was decreased in LOW treated ewes compared with CON and HIGH on d 15 (P < 0.05). Inflammatory responses included elevated rectal temperature on d 5 (P < 0.05) and serum cortisol concentrations in LPS-treated ewes on d 5 and d 15 (P < 0.05). Across LPS challenges, leukocyte responses were time-dependent, with pronounced differences at d 5 and d 15. On d 5, LPS-treated ewes exhibited delayed leukocyte response with reduced total white blood cell and increased lymphocyte and neutrophil concentrations at 24 h post-challenge compared with CON ewes (P < 0.05). No differences were detected on d 10 in leukocyte concentrations (P ≥ 0.2). On d 15, HIGH-LPS treated ewes exhibited late-phase leukocytosis, with increased total white blood cell concentrations at 24 h post-challenge compared with CON ewes (P < 0.05), accompanied by elevated neutrophil and lymphocyte concentrations (P < 0.05). Pregnancy rates were 100% across all treatment groups. Lamb growth and development were assessed from birth through weaning (d 60), with wool characteristics at weaning. Lamb birth weight (P = 0.4), average daily gain (P = 0.3), and adjusted weaning weight (P = 0.3) did not differ among maternal treatment groups. Lamb complete blood counts differed by maternal treatment at birth (d 0), with lambs born to LOW-LPS treated ewes exhibiting greater total white blood cell and neutrophil concentrations compared with lambs born to CON and HIGH ewes (P < 0.05). Wool fiber diameter did not differ among treatments at d 60 (P = 0.1); however, variation in fiber diameter tended to differ, with HIGH lambs compared with CON lambs (P = 0.05). Data suggest that repeated low-dose endotoxin exposure during the periconception period modulates maternal and neonatal immune parameters with minimal impacts on lamb performance.
